mainTopic: רבינא and רוניא's disputes over surrounding walls and דינא דבר מצרא; the משנה of the fallen courtyard wall; whether a borrower is believed that he paid early
overview: This amud opens with two stories about רבינא and his neighbor רוניא. In the first story, רבינא's fields surround רוניא's field on all sides. רבינא builds walls and asks רוניא to help pay, lowering his request each time, but רוניא refuses. When רוניא shouts over one cluster of dates, רבינא argues that this shows he wants his field protected. רבא then tells רוניא to pay at least a watchman's wage, or else be judged by the stricter ruling of רב הונא following רבי יוסי. In the second story, רב ספרא tells רבינא he cannot use דינא דבר מצרא to remove רוניא, because רוניא also borders the land. A new משנה then rules that neighbors must share the cost of rebuilding a fallen courtyard wall up to four אמות, and explains who is presumed to have paid. The גמרא begins with ריש לקיש, who says a borrower claiming he paid before the due date is not believed. אביי and רבא disagree, and their reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבינא surrounds רוניא and asks him to share the cost
steps.stepSummary: רבינא owns fields on all four sides of רוניא's field and builds walls. He asks for money three times, each time asking for less, and רוניא refuses every time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא's fields surrounded רוניא's field on all four sides. רבינא said: 'Give me your share of what I actually spent on the walls.' רוניא refused. 'Then pay your share at a cheap price of reeds.' He refused. 'Then at least pay what a watchman would cost.' He refused that too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a real-life case to show how the rules about surrounding walls work in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's requests go from most to least: the full actual cost, then a cheap price for reeds, then only a watchman's wage. רוניא refuses all three, so the question becomes whether he has to pay anything at all.

keyTerms.meaning: to build a wall or fence
reeds at a cheap price, the lowest cost of a fence

phrases.english: Ronya, Ravina surrounded him
on all four of his sides.
He said to him: "Give me according to how much I spent fencing,"
phrases.notes: He means half the real cost of the walls he built.

phrases.english: he did not give it to him.
"Give me according to the cheap price of reeds,"
he did not give it to him.
"Give me a watchman's wage,"
he did not give it to him.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a neighbor surrounded on all four sides refuses to pay anything toward the walls.

steps.title: The date-cluster incident
steps.stepSummary: While רוניא is harvesting dates, רבינא sends his אריס to take one cluster. רוניא shouts at him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day רוניא was harvesting his dates. רבינא told his sharecropper: 'Go take a cluster of dates from him.' The sharecropper went to take it, and רוניא shouted at him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. רבינא does something that tests how much רוניא cares about his crop, and this sets up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רוניא's angry reaction over a single cluster will be used as proof that he cares about protecting his dates, so the walls do help him.

keyTerms.meaning: a sharecropper who works a field for a share of the crop

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד הֲוָה קָא גָדֵר דִּיקְלֵי,
phrases.english: One day he was harvesting dates from his palms,
phrases.notes: Here גָדֵר means cutting down date clusters, not building a fence.

phrases.english: he (Ravina) said to his sharecropper:
Go take a cluster of dates from him.
He went to bring it, and Ronya shouted at him.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד הֲוָה קָא גָדֵר דִּיקְלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and sets up רבינא's proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רוניא protests even when a small amount of fruit is taken.

steps.title: רבינא: your shout shows you want protection
steps.stepSummary: רבינא argues that רוניא's protest shows he is glad to have his field protected. Even a goat would make guarding necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: 'You have shown that you are happy to have protection. Even if it were only a goat wandering in, wouldn't your field need guarding?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא uses רוניא's own shout as proof that the walls are worth something to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רוניא's position was that he does not need the walls, so he owes nothing. רבינא answers that someone who guards his dates this fiercely obviously wants his field protected, so he benefits from the walls.

keyTerms.meaning: you revealed what you really think
it is pleasing to you, you are happy with it

phrases.english: He said to him: You have revealed your mind
that it is pleasing to you
phrases.notes: He means you are happy to have the walls protecting your field.

phrases.english: even if it were only a mere goat,
wouldn't it need guarding?

steps.raayaObject: That רוניא benefits from the walls and so should pay
steps.raayaSupportSource: רוניא's own angry reaction to losing one date cluster

steps.title: רוניא: a goat just needs to be chased off
steps.stepSummary: רוניא pushes back. A goat does not require a wall, because you can simply chase it away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רוניא said: 'Just a goat? Doesn't it only need to be chased away?'
steps.whatsHappening: רוניא rejects רבינא's argument. He says protecting against a goat does not need walls at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רוניא agrees his field needs some protection, but he says a fence is not the needed kind. Shooing away an animal is enough, so he should not pay for walls.

phrases.english: He said to him: A mere goat,
doesn't it just need to be chased away?

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that guarding against a goat requires walls
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Chasing the goat away is enough, so walls are not needed

steps.title: רבינא: chasing still needs a person
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that even chasing a goat needs a man to do it. So רוניא owes at least the cost of a watchman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: 'But don't you need a man to chase it away?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רוניא's pushback. He says chasing away a goat still requires paying someone, which is exactly his lowest request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if walls are not needed, a guard is. The walls do the guard's job, so רוניא should at least pay a watchman's wage, the third and smallest request from the beginning of the story.

phrases.english: He said to him: And don't you need a man
to chase it away?

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Chasing away a goat costs nothing, so nothing is owed
steps.terutzMaskana: Chasing requires a hired man, so at least a watchman's wage is owed

steps.title: רבא's ruling: pay the watchman's wage or face the stricter law
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רוניא to settle with רבינא for the amount he will accept. Otherwise רבא will rule like רב הונא following רבי יוסי, which is stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא came before רבא. רבא said to רוניא: 'Go appease him with what he is willing to accept. If not, I will judge you like רב הונא's ruling following רבי יוסי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The case goes to court. רבא gives רוניא a choice: pay the small amount now, or be judged by the stricter rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא was willing to accept just a watchman's wage. If רוניא refuses, רבא will apply רב הונא's ruling following רבי יוסי, under which רוניא would have to pay based on what רבינא actually spent on the walls.

keyTerms.meaning: I will judge you by the strict law

steps.whatToRemember: A person surrounded on all sides benefits from his neighbor's walls. רבא pushes him to pay at least the watchman's wage, and holds the stricter full-cost ruling of רב הונא following רבי יוסי in reserve.

phrases.english: He came before Rava,
he (Rava) said to him (Ronya): Go appease him
with what he is willing to be appeased with;
phrases.notes: That means the watchman's wage, the smallest thing רבינא asked for.

phrases.english: and if not, I will judge you
like Rav Huna according to Rabbi Yosei.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The surrounded neighbor must pay. He can settle for the watchman's wage, or else he will be charged by the stricter rule of רב הונא following רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Second story: רבינא wants to use the neighbor's right
steps.stepSummary: רוניא buys land next to רבינא's property, and רבינא thinks he can remove him using דינא דבר מצרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רוניא bought land bordering רבינא's property. רבינא thought he could remove him because of the law giving a neighbor the first right to buy adjoining land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story about the same two men. This sets up רב ספרא's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under דינא דבר מצרא, a neighbor has first rights to buy land next to his own, and can remove an outside buyer. רבינא assumes this right lets him push רוניא out.

keyTerms.meaning: the law giving a neighbor first rights to buy adjoining land

phrases.english: Ronya bought land
on the border of Ravina's property.
Ravina thought to remove him
because of the law of the bordering neighbor;

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבינא assumes he can use דינא דבר מצרא to remove רוניא.

steps.title: רב ספרא: a big neighbor and a small neighbor are equal
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא בריה דרב ייבא quotes a folk saying to show רבינא he cannot remove רוניא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא, son of רב ייבא, said to רבינא: 'People say: four coins for a large hide, four coins for a small hide.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא rejects רבינא's plan with a popular saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רוניא also borders that land, though with a smaller field. A large hide and a small hide cost the same, and likewise a big neighbor has no stronger right than a small one. So רבינא cannot remove him.
steps.confusionAlert: רב ספרא is not saying the law of the bordering neighbor is wrong. He is saying it does not help רבינא here, because רוניא is also a bordering neighbor.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא לְרָבִינָא,
phrases.english: Rav Safra son of Rav Yeiva said to Ravina,
People say:
four for a large hide,
phrases.notes: Four coins either way. Big or small, it costs the same. Both of you are neighbors of that land.

phrases.english: four for a small hide.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי: אַרְבְּעָה לְצַלָּא, אַרְבְּעָה לְצַלָּלָא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבינא's plan to remove רוניא through דינא דבר מצרא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רוניא is also a bordering neighbor, and the size of a neighbor's field does not give him a stronger right
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A bordering neighbor cannot remove another bordering neighbor, even one with a smaller field.

steps.title: A fallen courtyard wall must be rebuilt together up to four cubits
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that when a shared courtyard wall falls, each neighbor can be forced to help rebuild it up to four אמות. Afterward the neighbor is presumed to have paid his share unless there is proof he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a wall between two courtyards fell, the court forces each neighbor to help rebuild it up to four אמות. Later, we assume he paid his share, unless the other brings proof that he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a basic rule: neighbors must share the cost of rebuilding a fallen courtyard wall up to four אמות. It also tells us who is believed about whether the money was paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four אמות is the height everyone is required to share. Because the court forces him to pay this much, we assume he did pay his part. So the neighbor who says he was not paid must bring proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'. It marks the start of a משנה
They obligate, meaning the court forces him
Presumed to be. This is what we assume unless someone proves otherwise

phrases.english: MISHNA: A courtyard wall that fell —
they obligate him to build it
up to four cubits.
He is presumed to have given,
phrases.notes: That's the neighbor who had to share the cost. We assume he paid his part.

phrases.english: unless he brings proof that he did not give.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story of רבינא and רוניא ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neighbors can be forced to share the cost of rebuilding a fallen courtyard wall up to four אמות. The neighbor is presumed to have paid unless proven otherwise.

steps.title: Above four cubits he pays only if he shows he wants the wall
steps.stepSummary: Above four אמות the neighbor is not forced to pay. If he builds another wall next to it, he must pay his share of the whole wall, even before he puts a roof on. In that case he is presumed not to have paid unless he proves he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: The court does not force him to pay for anything above four אמות. But if he built another wall next to it, even if he has not put a roof on it yet, he must pay for the whole wall. In that case we assume he did not pay, unless he brings proof that he did.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the part of the wall above four אמות. It gives one case where he must still pay, and it flips the presumption about who is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building a second wall next to the high wall shows he plans to use it, for example to put a roof over a room. So he must pay for all of it. Since nobody forced him to pay for the higher part, we do not assume he paid, and now he is the one who needs proof.

keyTerms.meaning: He leaned or built close to it
They roll onto him. He is charged for everything

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the presumption is reversed. Up to four אמות we assume he paid. For the extra height we assume he did not pay.
steps.whatToRemember: Up to four אמות: he must pay, and we assume he paid. Above four אמות: he pays only if he shows he wants the wall, and we assume he has not paid.

phrases.english: From four cubits and up —
they do not obligate him.
If he built another wall close to it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן עָלָיו אֶת הַתִּקְרָה –
phrases.english: even though he has not placed the roof on it —
they roll the whole thing onto him.
phrases.notes: He has to pay his share of the entire wall, including the part above four cubits.

phrases.english: He is presumed not to have given,
unless he brings proof that he gave.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וּלְמַעְלָן אֵין מְחַיְּיבִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from the required height to the extra height.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Above four אמות he does not have to pay unless he builds an adjoining wall. Then he pays for the whole wall and is presumed not to have paid unless he brings proof.

steps.title: A borrower who says he paid early is not believed
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that if a loan had a set due date, and the borrower says 'I paid you before the due date,' he is not believed. People hardly ever pay before the due date.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: if someone set a due date for a loan, and the borrower says, 'I paid you before my due date,' he is not believed. The lender would be glad if he even paid on time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a statement from ריש לקיש about believing a borrower who claims he paid early. This begins a discussion about when someone is believed to have paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's reasoning is about normal behavior. Borrowers usually do not pay early, and many do not even pay on time. So a claim of early payment is not trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא. It marks the start of the גמרא's discussion
One who sets a due date

phrases.english: GEMARA: Reish Lakish said:
One who sets a due date for his fellow,
and the borrower said to him:
"I paid you within my time" —
phrases.notes: This means before the due date arrived.

phrases.english: he is not believed;
if only he would pay on time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ הַקּוֹבֵעַ זְמַן לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה with a related rule about when a claim of payment is believed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrower who claims he paid before the due date is not believed.

steps.title: אביי and רבא say people do sometimes pay early
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא disagree with ריש לקיש. They say people do sometimes pay before the due date, because when money happens to come in, a person decides to pay off his debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both said: people do pay before the due date. Sometimes money happens to come his way, and he says, 'Let me go pay him back.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא push back on ריש לקיש's assumption that people do not normally pay early. Their reasoning is cut off at the end of this amud and continues on the next one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's ruling depends on the idea that early payment is unusual. אביי and רבא challenge that idea directly: when a person has spare money, he may want to clear his debt. If early payment is normal, the borrower's claim becomes believable.

keyTerms.meaning: A person tends to do this. It describes normal behavior

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both say:
A person is apt to pay within his time —
sometimes money happens to come to him,
he says: I will go pay it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ עֲבִיד אִינִישׁ דְּפָרַע בְּגוֹ זִימְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with ריש לקיש's assumption about how borrowers behave.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects ריש לקיש's assumption that borrowers do not pay before the due date.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ריש לקיש overlooks that a borrower who happens to have money may choose to pay early.
